accuracy.title: An accurate reading starts with accurate ganji
accuracy.sub: A Saju reading has two stages: computing the ganji (the chart) and interpreting it. If the foundation — the ganji — is wrong, even the most eloquent interpretation is ultimately nonsense.
accuracy.band.title: Ask ChatGPT for your Saju, and the chart itself comes out wrong
accuracy.band.desc: Chat AIs can't compute the perpetual calendar — they merely guess your ganji in a plausible-sounding way. And with the wrong chart, the entire reading describes someone else's destiny. Tao Fortune first builds your chart from a precision calendar database — the 60 ganji, 24 solar terms, and lunar–solar conversion all accounted for — then lets AI handle only the interpretation.
accuracy.band.more: Why we're more accurate — learn more
accuracy.step.title: A reading has two stages
accuracy.step.1.d: Setting the four pillars (year, month, day, hour ganji) from your birth data. This is astronomy and calendar math — there is exactly one correct answer.
accuracy.step.2.d: Interpreting wealth, love, health and more from the chart. This is where rich language and insight matter.
accuracy.step.note: If ① is wrong, ② becomes “eloquently written nonsense.” The accurate foundation must come first.
accuracy.why.title: Why do LLMs so often get ganji wrong?
accuracy.why.lead: LLMs like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are writers, not calculators. They produce fluent prose, but are structurally weak at precise astronomical and arithmetic computation.
accuracy.why.1.t: Solar terms are astronomy, not the calendar
accuracy.why.1.d: The year pillar changes at ipchun, not Jan 1; the month pillar changes at the 24 solar terms. These moments are fixed by the sun's ecliptic longitude and differ to the minute each year. Approximating them breaks the month pillar on boundary dates.
accuracy.why.2.d: Lunar month lengths and leap months are set by actual new moons and solar terms — astronomical events with no closed formula, requiring precise tables. LLMs can't reproduce them reliably.
accuracy.why.3.t: The day pillar is cumulative arithmetic
accuracy.why.3.d: The day pillar is the total days since an epoch, mod 60. Faking tens of thousands of days of integer math “in your head” means a single day's error flips the entire day pillar.
accuracy.why.4.d: An LLM states a wrong ganji as fluently as a right one and never checks its own work — producing results that look authoritative but are wrong.
accuracy.our.title: So here's how Tao Fortune does it
accuracy.our.1.d: We compute your chart from a precise perpetual-calendar database with solar terms, true solar time and lunar–solar conversion built in — equally accurate whether you enter a solar or lunar date.
accuracy.our.2.d: Only on a correctly built chart does the AI add deep interpretation. The AI focuses on what it does best — rich reading — not computation.
accuracy.our.quote: “Rich interpretation on an accurate foundation.” That is what a truly accurate reading requires.
